x: We were drawn on the outside but after the initial breakaway Archie Bedford was seen to be lying second and Eddie Short was also well up. At the half-distance the latter was in fourth place but there was no sign of Archie, and it later transpired that he had dropped out owing to shoe trouble at abou…
Eddie Short ran the best of our men with Bill Lucas showing next best time and Steve Charlton and Tom Carter, despite a fall over a bicycle during his "leg," also ran well.

Owing to the numerous barring clauses our team was well below our usual strength and then Eddie Short after being in the first twenty at the half-distance suffered an injury to his ankle and although pluckily completing the course he finished well down the field.
Walker allowed Green to hand over with him at the end of the third stage, but Archie Bedford, Eddie Short and Bill Lucas saw to it that we maintained our unbeaten record for this race.

Walker just beat Eddie Short for second place, and then came Jack Braughton 5th, Bill Lucas 7th, Archie Bedford 9th and Len Herbert 11th. All the first five were selected to run for Surrey in the Inter-Counties race at York, and Jack Brown 7th in the Kent race and A.
Hudson 6th, Len Adams 5th, Eric Herbert 6th, Len Herbert 4th, Len Bishop 4th, with Eddie Short taking us into the lead on the 9th stage, for Chas.
Eddie Short ran our final lap of about 3 miles, and although he caught Butler, of Surrey A.C., he was eventually beaten on the final run-in by about a yard.

Mike Stearman ran well to finish 5th and our lads packed well in the 'teens so that scoring 12 a side we came out on top by a comfortable margin. Placings and times of our members were as under:—1, Tooby, 30.4; 5, Stearman, 30.16; 7, Short, 30.32; 10, Taylor, 30.51; 12, E.
Walker put in a really fine run to put them in the lead on the 3rd stage, and this was maintained by Wright, Short, Lucas and Bedford down to the end of the 7th relay.
Herbert, 24.42 ; Burr, 24.33 ; Short, 24.31 ; Bedford, 24.23.
By the top of Copse Hill Herbert had moved right through the field and four others, Walker, Smart, Short and Tooby went down the hill together.

Short took over at 3 miles and then Maynard came through at about 4 miles and strolled home untroubled. Cliff Roffey came through for second, Short 3rd., Walker 5th and then the pack Bagnall, Gebbett, Burr, Brickwood and Trower 7th to 11th to make sure of the team race.

Barratt of Ealing was an easy winner in 43.17, followed by Olney 44.13, and Ingles another minute back, third Peter Bagnall ran well to be 4th in 45.42, but he had no backing from the rest who included Short 9th, Gebbett 12th, Abbott 13th, L.

After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.
Short, Bagnall and Patterson, please oblige. It will be noted that the post-war boom in athletics shows itself in performances by club members.

Knight of Essex Beagles was the individual winner completing the course in record time and finishing in front of Sando. Pete Bagnall was our first man home in 11th position and supported by Masters, Short and L. Bishop, we gained 3rd place in the team event.
Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
He was accompanied over the first five miles by Pat Newell, followed by Walker, Bagnall, Short and Gebbett, but at this stage Short retired.
These four opened up a short gap from George Davidson. When the second lap of the Common was completed, Walker was again leading and Flanagan was beginning to feel the effects of the fast pace.
Then followed a string of runners before we again saw a Belgrave vest filled by Eddie Short who had John Moore and Jumbo Masters close on his heels, all of them in the 130's.

At the end of the first lap Clive Shippen was leading with Moore and Short well in attendance. A quick check showed that we were well in the lead and should have no difficulty in holding our position.
